headline: High-risk default interaction: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer data can feed Mentat’s filesystem-backed coding workflow, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and Mentat reads files passed on the command line with filesystem-backed shared state. If Chatwoot content is copied into files or prompts, Mentat may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default operator workflows, though not proven automatic.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into files that Mentat reads as task context
IF Mentat is run on content originating from customer messages or reports
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Mentat task files
Use a separate review step for any pasted customer text
Prefix imported text with a non-executable delimiter
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content
requires-engineering: enforce prompt/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while Mentat reads and writes local files and sends context to a configured model provider. If shared workspace files contain Chatwoot data, Mentat can upload that content to a third party during normal operation. This is a default-path leakage risk, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF Chatwoot artifacts are placed in files Mentat opens
IF Mentat forwards those files to its model provider during assistance
mitigations: Do not place customer records in Mentat working directories
Redact sensitive fields before opening files in Mentat
Use a separate non-sensitive sample project for coding help
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before model calls
requires-engineering: isolate Chatwoot data from Mentat storage paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has write_filesystem and modify_git_state with filesystem-based shared state across instances. Chatwoot is a runnable open-source support system with broad network egress and likely operational file/state surfaces. If both operate on the same workspace or repo, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide without locking, making destructive overwrite or inconsistent state likely in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree
IF Mentat instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
requires-engineering: add workspace-level mutexes
requires-engineering: route edits through a merge queue

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing content and reports, and Mentat is a coding assistant that can turn file content into edits. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative task input, Mentat may propagate errors into code or configuration without verification. The pair creates a plausible A-to-B trust chain, but not an automatic action-taking loop.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is used as the source of truth for Mentat tasks
IF Mentat applies edits without an independent validation step
mitigations: Require human review before applying Mentat diffs
Cross-check Chatwoot-derived facts against source systems
Limit Mentat to refactoring non-semantic changes
requires-engineering: add validation gates before edit application
requires-engineering: separate fact extraction from code editing

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Mentat sends selected file contents to a configured model provider and handles API keys. If customer data or regulated records enter Mentat’s context, residency and retention obligations can diverge from Chatwoot’s support workflow. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a moderate compliance-risk finding.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is copied into Mentat-managed files
IF the configured model provider retains prompts outside Chatwoot policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Mentat prompts and files
Use synthetic or anonymized examples for coding help
Review provider retention settings before use
requires-engineering: document a shared retention policy
requires-engineering: enforce residency controls in the workflow
